PAPERS.short: Zhang wildfire smoke waves long-term PM2.5 cardiovascular hospitalisation Medicare 2026
PAPERS.title: Impact of wildfire smoke waves on the association between long-term exposure to fine particulate matter and cardiovascular hospitalizations among older adults in the United States
PAPERS.pm: Two-year mean PM2.5 (1 km ML model) and smoke PM2.5 (10 km); smoke wave = >=2 d with smoke PM2.5 >10 ug/m3
PAPERS.endpoint: First hospitalisation: overall CVD, IHD, cerebrovascular disease, hypertension
PAPERS.n: 65.2 million Medicare beneficiaries aged >=65, 2017-2022, ZIP-year quasi-Poisson. Raising two-year PM2.5 from 5 to 9 ug/m3 (WHO guideline to US standard) gave overall CVD RR 1.09 (1.09-1.10) in ZIP-years without smoke waves but 1.04 (1.03-1.04) with them (ratio of RRs 1.05, 1.04-1.06); the pattern held below 9 ug/m3 and was stronger in men, urban and western residents. Limitation: the attenuation is what one expects if smoke spikes inflate the two-year mean with a less toxic-per-mass or differently distributed exposure, so this is an exposure-metric artefact as much as a biological finding; ZIP-level assignment and 10 km smoke grids blur the contrast. Relevance: high - long-term means hide episodic peaks that only high-frequency network data resolve.

PAPERS.short: Zendi brown carbon wood pyrolysis tracers cytotoxicity A549 2026
PAPERS.title: Fine Brown Carbon Aerosol Emitted by Wood Pyrolysis - New Harmful Tracers and Cytotoxicity in Human Lung Cells
PAPERS.pm: Fine brown carbon from 350 C wood pyrolysis; water, methanol and acetone extracts
PAPERS.endpoint: A549 metabolic activity, membrane damage, death phenotype
PAPERS.n: Smouldering-regime BrC was generated by 350 C wood pyrolysis, extracted in three solvents and characterised by UHPLC-ESI-ToF-MS non-target analysis (776-1,132 molecular features per extract). Water extracts were dominated by lignin phenols and aromatic acids; methanol and acetone pulled less oxidised terpenoid and sterol-like species. Cytotoxicity in A549 cells ranked water < methanol < acetone, consistent with lipophilic, membrane-partitioning and redox-active compounds; named contributors to baseline narcosis included 3-hydroxybenzoic, salicylic and p-coumaric acids, benzene-1,2,4-triol and coniferylaldehyde. Limitation: solvent extracts at unreported dose-equivalence to inhaled mass, a single carcinoma line, and pyrolysis rather than flaming or aged smoke. Relevance: low-medium - supports BrC (UV-absorbing) channels as a toxicity-weighted metric.

PAPERS.short: de Luna wildfire PM toxicity systematic review 2026
PAPERS.title: Systematic review on the toxicity of wildfire emitted particulate matter: State of science, knowledge gaps and way forward
PAPERS.endpoint: In vitro and in vivo toxicity endpoints
PAPERS.n: 46 in vitro and in vivo studies, 2005-2025 (epidemiology excluded). Only 42% of in vitro and 27% of in vivo studies used PM actually collected during wildfires; the rest used surrogate burns. In vitro work concentrates on lung (50%) and macrophages (17%); inhalation studies on lung (46%), heart (15%) and brain (15%). Mechanisms reported are mainly inflammation, oxidative stress and DNA damage, and toxicity varied with dose, size, fuel and burn condition. Gaps: incomplete physicochemical characterisation, unrealistic doses, few chronic or toxicokinetic studies, no work on mixtures with urban pollution. Limitation: no quantitative synthesis or risk-of-bias grading, so heterogeneity is described, not explained. Relevance: medium - the field cannot yet say which smoke property a sensor should track beyond mass.

PAPERS.short: Ruan gut microbiota dose-time trajectories PM2.5 PFOS mouse 2026
PAPERS.title: Time-resolved profiling reveals nonlinear dose-time trajectories of gut microbiota in PM2.5 and PFOS exposure models
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 inhalation at multiple dose levels (separate PFOS drinking-water model)
PAPERS.n: Two mouse models (PM2.5 inhalation; PFOS in drinking water) sampled repeatedly across dose levels and exposure stages, with 16S sequencing and generalised additive models for dose-time structure. Controls showed clear temporal succession, which the authors stress must be modelled before attributing change to exposure. In the PM2.5 model, restructuring peaked at early-to-intermediate stages, with nonlinear trajectories in Lactobacillus, Prevotella and the Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio; PFOS effects were later and longer. No effect sizes with CIs are reported in the abstract. Limitation: functional pathways are inferred, not measured; doses and particle source are not given in the abstract, and cage effects dominate small murine microbiome studies. Relevance: low - mechanistic, but the time-varying response argues against single-timepoint toxicology.

PAPERS.short: Harb idiopathic subglottic stenosis geographic clustering ecological 2026
PAPERS.title: Geographic Clustering of Idiopathic Subglottic Stenosis in North America: An Ecological Cohort Study
PAPERS.pm: State/province PM2.5 alongside temperature, humidity and elevation
PAPERS.endpoint: Survey-ascertained iSGS prevalence per million White females
PAPERS.n: 4,450 members of an online iSGS support group (99.3% female) mapped to state/province and scaled by census White female populations. Prevalence clustered in dry, high, warm areas: Wyoming 18.1, Utah 17.4, Colorado 13.9 per million vs New Hampshire 1.2; Alberta 85.4 vs Quebec 2.9. PM2.5 was not independently associated with prevalence but modified the elevation association. Limitation: the numerator is self-selected membership of an online group, so 'prevalence' reflects diagnosis, awareness and referral patterns; state-level ecology cannot separate climate from health-system access. Level 4 evidence by the authors' own grading. Relevance: low - a null for PM at state scale, hypothesis-generating only.

PAPERS.short: Hahad exposome heart failure older adults review 2026
PAPERS.title: Exposomic Determinants in Heart Failure Among Older Adults - Mechanistic Links, Clinical Evidence, and Future Perspectives
PAPERS.pm: Air pollution (PM) within a multi-exposure exposome (noise, heat, metals, light at night, greenness)
PAPERS.endpoint: Heart failure incidence, decompensation and prognosis
PAPERS.n: Narrative review arguing for a life-course, systems-level view of heart failure in older adults in which air pollution sits alongside traffic noise, temperature extremes, metals, artificial light at night and social environment. Mechanisms proposed to converge on oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammaging, impaired autophagy, epigenetic change and senescence, lowering the threshold for HF onset and decompensation. No new data or pooled estimates. Limitation: the mechanistic convergence is asserted from separate literatures; co-exposures (PM, noise, heat) are spatially correlated, and the review does not address how to separate them. Relevance: low - multi-exposure co-located sensing (PM, noise, temperature) is what the exposome framing would need.

PAPERS.short: Kou Xing Su San Sang Xing Tang PM2.5 lung injury rats 2026
PAPERS.title: Xing Su San and Sang Xing Tang attenuate PM2.5-induced lung injury and inflammatory marker expression in rats
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 inhalation 500 ug/m3, 3 h/day, 28 days, under warm-dry or cool-dry conditions
PAPERS.endpoint: Lung RAGE mRNA, NF-kB p65, S100A9-positive cells
PAPERS.n: 40 male Wistar rats in five groups of 8. PM2.5 at 500 ug/m3 raised lung RAGE mRNA 2.8-fold (warm-dry) and 2.5-fold (cool-dry), NF-kB p65 2.4- and 2.2-fold, and S100A9-positive cells to 3.45% and 3.13% vs 0.82% in controls (all P<0.05). The two herbal formulas, given by gavage, partly reversed these markers in their matched climate model (e.g. RAGE 1.6-fold with Sang Xing Tang). Limitation: 500 ug/m3 is an episode-level dose, n=8 per group, no histology scoring or blinding reported, and formula composition is not standardised. Relevance: low - a temperature-humidity x PM interaction in toxicology, not monitoring.

PAPERS.short: de la Cruz automated forced air injection cordwood stove PM2.5 particle size 2026
PAPERS.title: Less Mass of PM2.5 Emissions, Smaller Particles: The Trade-Off of Automated Forced Air Injection in a Residential Cordwood Stove
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 mass emission and particle size distribution
PAPERS.endpoint: Stove PM2.5 emission and size distribution
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract was available from PubMed, Europe PMC, Crossref or Semantic Scholar at harvest. The title reports that automated forced-air injection in a residential cordwood stove lowers PM2.5 mass emissions but shifts particles to smaller sizes. No numbers, test protocol or fuel details can be summarised. Limitation: cannot be appraised from the title; the trade-off claim needs number-based metrics to evaluate. Relevance: high in principle - a mass reduction with a shift to ultrafine sizes is precisely the case where optical mass sensors, blind below ~0.3 um, would overstate the improvement.

PAPERS.short: Tsai mineral dust biomass burning aerosol convergence East Asia western North Pacific 2026
PAPERS.title: Convergence of mineral dust and biomass-burning aerosols over East Asia and the western North Pacific
PAPERS.pm: Mixed mineral dust and biomass-burning aerosol (transport)
PAPERS.endpoint: Co-occurrence and transport of dust and smoke
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract was available at harvest from any route tried. The title describes convergence of mineral dust and biomass-burning aerosol over East Asia and the western North Pacific, presumably from observation and transport analysis; the instruments, period and metrics cannot be stated. Limitation: not appraisable. Relevance: medium in principle - mixed dust-smoke plumes combine coarse non-spherical and fine absorbing particles, a regime where optical sensor size and refractive-index assumptions fail together.

PAPERS.short: Mulena dust intrusion regimes north-central Argentina vertical structure optical properties 2026
PAPERS.title: Dust intrusion regimes over north-central Argentina: Vertical structure, optical properties, and transport pathways
PAPERS.pm: Mineral dust aerosol vertical profiles and optical properties
PAPERS.endpoint: Dust intrusion regimes and transport pathways
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract at harvest. The title describes a classification of dust-intrusion regimes over north-central Argentina by vertical structure, optical properties and transport pathway, likely from lidar or sun-photometer records with trajectory analysis. No data can be summarised. Limitation: not appraisable; column and vertical optical properties do not by themselves give surface PM. Relevance: low-medium - dust-regime classification is the prior a satellite-surface fusion model needs for coarse-mode episodes in an under-monitored region.
